title: Rafael and the Veil
premise: Ulyana Coldharbour makes her living bottling other people's memories in Veymark, a city where magic is outlawed and memory-charms are the only contraband worth dying for. When she steals a charm from a stranger named Rafael, she discovers his memories are missing entirely — replaced by pages from a century-old book of prophecies that name tonight's date as the night the Veiled King wakes. The prophecy insists that a thief with no past of her own must unbind the king from the entity wearing his crown, and Ulyana realizes Rafael is not a man but a vessel the Veil has been building for a hundred years. As the city's witch-hunters close in and the Veil devours more of Rafael's borrowed self, Ulyana must choose between restoring her own stolen childhood memories or using them as the key to sever the king's binding. In the end she gives up her past to free them both, and the found family she built along the way helps her begin making new memories worth keeping.
about_author: Marguerite Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes about thieves, ghosts, and the things families bury, from a house full of books that may or may not be haunted.

chapters.title: The Charm That Bit Back
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the eve of the city's Remembrance Festival, Ulyana lifts a memory-charm from a quiet stranger named Rafael, only to find it contains no memories at all — just a page of prophecy naming tonight's date. Her fence refuses to touch it. Emotional beat: unease; the first crack in her carefully ordinary life.

chapters.title: A Hundred Years of Tonight
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She breaks into the sealed archive of the Order of the Quill and finds the original prophecy book: every page blank except one, which describes her theft in detail written a century ago. Witch-hunters raid the archive; Rafael appears and pulls her out through a door that shouldn't exist. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Veil Wears
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael confesses he woke three days ago with no past, only instructions, and shows Ulyana the crown-shaped scar on his palm where the Veil anchors itself. They learn the 'king' is a beloved monarch slowly hollowed by the entity. Beat: reluctant partnership; two people with nothing but each other's company.

chapters.title: The Kitchen at the End of the Row
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hiding in the tenement kitchen of Marisol, an exiled hedge-witch who once bought Ulyana's charms, they gather allies: Marisol, her foster-son Tam, and a disgraced witch-hunter named Oskar. For one evening they are almost a family. Beat: warmth and found family, deliberately placed before the fall.

chapters.title: Remembrance
chapters.summary: Oskar's POV. During the festival, the Veiled King appears in public and the crowd's joy curdles as the Veil feeds on collective memory. Oskar sees his own forgotten sister's face in the king's retinue and defects, bringing the Order's secret: the binding can only be cut from inside the crown. Beat: horror and betrayal of the state.

chapters.title: The Price of a Past
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The prophecy's final page reveals the unbinding requires memories freely surrendered by someone with none of their own — meaning Ulyana must give up the stolen childhood memories she has hoarded for ten years, the only proof of who she was. She refuses. Beat: denial; the theme of inheritance made personal.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Desperate to protect Marisol, Tam secretly offers the Veil his memories in Ulyana's place, and the exchange begins to unravel him. Ulyana catches him mid-ritual and tears the bargain apart, but the Veil now knows where they hide. Beat: guilt, sacrifice, the cost of love.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Hunted through the palace's memory-warped halls, the group reaches the throne room, where the king begs silently for release while the Veil wears his smile. Rafael learns he was grown from the king's discarded grief — he is the prophecy's loophole and its bait. Beat: climax rising; identity as weapon.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the crown, Ulyana pours her hoarded childhood — her mother's voice, her first theft, her real name — into the binding and severs it. The Veil, starved, collapses inward; the king dies human and grateful; Rafael survives, finally empty in a way that can be filled. Beat: climax; grief and triumph entwined.

chapters.title: New Memory
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue-like. Weeks later, magic is still outlawed but quietly tolerated; Marisol reopens her kitchen, Oskar burns his hunter's oath, and Rafael begins remembering — starting with Ulyana. She keeps a single empty charm-bottle on the shelf, waiting to be filled with something chosen rather than stolen. Beat: resolution; found family endures, and the future is unwritten.
